extracted.intended_audience: arXiv authors, readers, volunteer moderators, and arXiv administrative staff
extracted.subtask_description: Screening and handling of preprint submissions to arXiv for correct category assignment, technical compliance, and policy-appropriate content prior to announcement/posting. Describes moderator roles, workflow, timelines, and removal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to the scientific community / appropriate content
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be relevant to the scientific community and follow arXiv policies; content should generally describe work that would be refereeable by a conventional journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The moderation process checks that submissions are relevant to the scientific community. ‘Appropriate content’ is further characterized as content that would be refereeable by a conventional journal. Moderators evaluate submissions against these expectations when deciding whether to post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with arXiv policies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators and administrators review submissions to ensure they conform to arXiv policies (policy guidance comes from the Scientific Director, Scientific Advisory Board, and Subject Advisory Committees). Noncompliance can trigger additional review or holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct subject category and classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submission must be classified to the appropriate subject category and sub-category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators and administrators check classification and metadata to confirm the submission is assigned to the appropriate subject area (arXiv has 8 scientific categories and 149 sub-categories). Misclassification can lead to reassignment or flagging for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical requirements: formatting and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must meet arXiv's technical requirements, including correct formatting and metadata information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software-supported checks and human review confirm formatting and metadata compliance. Technical issues can cause a submission to be flagged and potentially placed on hold until resolved prior to announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-article format expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Content should be in the format of a research article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The moderation process expects submissions to be presented as research articles; submissions that do not match this format may be flagged as inappropriate for arXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation is not peer review; no evaluation of scientific validity
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv moderation is not a peer-review process and moderators/staff do not evaluate the validity of the scientific process or provide feedback on submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators check classification, technical compliance, and appropriateness, but they do not assess scientific validity or offer substantive feedback on the research. This is stated explicitly to set expectations for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging for additional action or review
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 15% of daily submissions are flagged for additional actions or review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are flagged when issues arise with category assignment, technical requirements, or content appropriateness. Flagged items require human moderator or administrator attention and are resolved prior to announcement or placed on hold if unresolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution timeline / announcement schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal to resolve moderation issues within 24 hours; submissions resolved before the deadline are posted to the next announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the goal is 24-hour resolution, some decisions require more time; in such cases the submission is placed on hold until a decision is reached. Daily deadline for resolving flagged submissions is 14:00 Eastern Time for moderators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold policy while a decision is pending
rubrics_metrics.description: If a moderation decision cannot be reached before the announcement deadline, the submission is placed on hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held submissions are not announced until the issue is resolved. This balances arXiv's goals of rapid distribution with moderation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanence and removal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Once posted, submissions generally cannot be removed; removal is considered only if the submitter did not have the legal right to submit the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv is a permanent repository. Content posted in error that would otherwise have been rejected remains permanent except in legal-rights cases (e.g., copyright/ownership issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderator selection and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderators are volunteers selected by the Subject Advisory Committee based on expertise in their professional fields and subject classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators evaluate submissions for their assigned sub-categories. They operate under guidance from the Scientific Director and advisory committees; Chairs and the Director help resolve questions when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderator assignment, collaboration, and workload expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderators are each responsible for submissions to their assigned sub-category and ideally work with at least one other moderator; they generally spend less than 30 minutes each day resolving flagged submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some categories may only have one moderator. Moderators are volunteers from around the world; the workflow expects rapid handling of flags within the daily deadline (14:00 ET). Administrators and volunteer moderators collaborate to review and resolve issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of software support in checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderation uses software support to confirm classification and technical compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated checks assist moderators and administrators by flagging classification mismatches, formatting errors, and metadata problems, which are then reviewed by humans as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative oversight and escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv administrators and moderators work under guidance from the Scientific Director, Scientific Advisory Board, and Subject Advisory Committees, with escalation paths for difficult cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chair of the Subject Advisory Committees and the Scientific Director help administrators and moderators resolve questions and issues when requested; complex or ambiguous cases are escalated for advisory input.
